message.content:
Based on my search, here are the typical jersey numbers for linebackers in football:

## NFL Linebacker Numbers

Under current NFL rules (as of 2023), linebackers can wear numbers in the range of **0–59 and 90–99**.

### Historical Evolution:
- **1973 (original rules)**: Linebackers wore **50–59**
- **1984**: Linebackers were also allowed **90–99** (if 50–59 was unavailable)
- **2015**: Linebackers were allowed **40–49**
- **2021–2023**: Major expansion allowing **0–59 and 90–99**, including single-digit numbers and zero

### Traditional/Classic Linebacker Numbers:
While the rules have expanded, traditionally linebackers are most commonly associated with:
- **50–59** (the classic range)
- **90–99** (particularly for outside linebackers and edge rushers)

### Examples of Linebacker Numbers:
- **40–49**: Often worn by linebackers (e.g., Devin White wore #40 at LSU)
- **50–59**: Classic middle linebacker numbers (e.g., #50–#59)
- **90–99**: Common for outside linebackers/defensive ends in 3-4 schemes

## College Football

College football has much more flexible numbering rules. While the NFL has strict position-based numbering, college players can generally wear any number from 0–99, with the only major restriction being that at least five offensive linemen must wear 50–79.

## Summary Table

| Level | Linebacker Number Range |
|-------|------------------------|
| NFL (current) | 0–59, 90–99 |
| NFL (traditional) | 50–59, 90–99 |
| College | 0–99 (very flexible) |

The 2021–2023 rule changes have made NFL numbering much more flexible, so you're now seeing linebackers with single-digit numbers (like #0, #1, #4) that would have been unheard of in earlier eras.

Sources:
1. https://operations.nfl.com/the-rules/rules-changes/nfl-jersey-numbers/
2. https://touchdowntrips.com/nfl-jersey-numbers-explained/
3. https://www.jt-sw.com/football/pro/index.nsf/Documents/0-jers-nums
4. https://www.metroleague.org/nfl-jersey-numbers-list_af/
